## components/Analytics.tsx

````tsx
'use client';
import { useEffect } from 'react';
export default function Analytics() {
  useEffect(() => {
    const id = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_GA4_ID;
    if (!id || !/^G-[A-Z0-9]+$/.test(id)) return;
    const load = () => {
      window.dataLayer = window.dataLayer || [];
      window.gtag = (...args: unknown[]) => window.dataLayer!.push(args);
      window.gtag('js', new Date());
      window.gtag('config', id, { send_page_view: false });
      window.gtag('event', 'page_view', {
        page_location: location.origin + location.pathname,
        page_path: location.pathname,
      });
      const s = document.createElement('script');
      s.src = 'https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=' + id;
      s.async = true;
      document.head.appendChild(s);
    };
    window.addEventListener('pointerdown', load, { once: true });
    return () => window.removeEventListener('pointerdown', load);
  }, []);
  return null;
}
````

## components/Calculator.tsx

````tsx
'use client';
import { useEffect, useId, useState, useRef, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import {
  emptyState,
  evaluateTool,
  restoreState,
  surfaces,
  type ToolKind,
  type ToolState,
  type ToolResult,
} from '@/lib/calc/ui';
import { number, money } from '@/lib/format';
import { track } from '@/lib/analytics';
import { FormulaBox, ResultCard } from './Modules';
import ShapeDiagram from './ShapeDiagram';
import QuoteCTA from './QuoteCTA';
import { initialToolState, priceBook, hasPrice, sealcoatPresets, defaultBook } from '@/lib/data';
const human = (text: string) => text.replace(/-/g, ' ').replace(/^./, (x) => x.toUpperCase());
type Props = { kind: ToolKind; slug: string; surface?: string; material?: string };
export default function Calculator({
  kind,
  slug,
  surface = 'asphalt',
  material = 'material',
}: Props) {
  const [state, setState] = useState<ToolState>(() => initialToolState(kind, material));
  const [result, setResult] = useState<ToolResult | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState('');
  const [message, setMessage] = useState('');
  const id = useId();
  const outputRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const currentPrice = priceBook[surface];
  const pricingAvailable = hasPrice(surface);
  const densityKey =
    material === 'pea gravel'
      ? 'peaGravelDensity'
      : material === 'rock'
        ? 'rockDensity'
        : material === 'crusher run'
          ? 'crusherRunDensity'
          : material === 'road base'
            ? 'roadBaseDensity'
            : material === 'asphalt'
              ? 'asphaltDensity'
              : null;
  useEffect(() => {
    const raw = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('inputs');
    if (raw)
      try {
        const shared = restoreState(raw);
        setState(shared);
        setResult(evaluateTool(kind, shared, surface));
      } catch (e) {
        setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Invalid shared inputs.');
      }
  }, [kind, surface]);
  function change(next: ToolState) {
    setState(next);
    setResult(null);
    setError('');
    setMessage('');
  }
  function field(key: string, val: string) {
    change({ ...state, fields: { ...state.fields, [key]: val } });
  }
  function calculate(event: FormEvent) {
    event.preventDefault();
    try {
      const r = evaluateTool(kind, state, surface);
      setResult(r);
      setError('');
      track('calculator_used', slug);
      track('result_viewed', slug);
      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        outputRef.current?.focus({ preventScroll: true });
        if (matchMedia('(max-width: 940px)').matches)
          outputRef.current?.scrollIntoView({
            behavior: matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches ? 'auto' : 'smooth',
            block: 'start',
          });
      });
    } catch (e) {
      setResult(null);
      setError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Check the inputs.');
    }
  }
  const input = (key: string, label: string, unit: string, required = true, help?: string) => (
    <label className="field" key={key}>
      <span>
        {label}
        {!required && <small> Optional</small>}
      </span>
      <div className="input-wrap">
        <input
          name={key}
          type="number"
          step="any"
          min={['waste', 'compaction'].includes(key) ? '0' : undefined}
          value={state.fields[key] ?? ''}
          onChange={(e) => field(key, e.target.value)}
          required={required}
          aria-describedby={help ? `${id}-${key}-help` : undefined}
        />
        <span>{unit}</span>
      </div>
      {help && <small id={`${id}-${key}-help`}>{help}</small>}
    </label>
  );
  const checkbox = (key: string, label: string) => (
    <label className="check">
      <input
        type="checkbox"
        checked={state.fields[key] === 'true'}
        onChange={(e) => {
          if (e.target.checked && (key === 'removal' || key === 'base')) {
            const low = currentPrice?.[key + 'Low'],
              high = currentPrice?.[key + 'High'];
            change({
              ...state,
              fields: {
                ...state.fields,
                [key]: 'true',
                [key + 'Low']: low?.verified && low.value !== null ? String(low.value) : '',
                [key + 'High']: high?.verified && high.value !== null ? String(high.value) : '',
              },
            });
          } else field(key, String(e.target.checked));
        }}
      />
      {label}
    </label>
  );
  const cost = kind === 'cost' || kind === 'compare';
  async function copy(text: string) {
    try {
      await navigator.clipboard.writeText(text);
      setMessage('Copied to clipboard.');
    } catch {
      setMessage('Copy is unavailable in this browser.');
    }
  }
  const share = () => {
    const url = new URL(location.href);
    url.search = '';
    url.searchParams.set('inputs', JSON.stringify(state));
    history.replaceState(null, '', url);
    void copy(url.toString());
  };
  return (
    <div className="calculator-shell" id="calculator">
      <form className="calculator-inputs" onSubmit={calculate}>
        <div className="panel-heading">
          <span className="eyebrow">
            01 /{' '}
            {surface === 'repair'
              ? 'Patch area'
              : surface === 'concrete-repair'
                ? 'Resurfacing area'
                : 'Your measurements'}
          </span>
          <span className="unit-badge">US units</span>
        </div>
        {kind === 'converter' ? (
          <>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Conversion direction</span>
              <select
                value={state.fields.direction ?? 'yards-to-tons'}
                onChange={(e) => field('direction', e.target.value)}
              >
                <option value="yards-to-tons">Cubic yards to short tons</option>
                <option value="tons-to-yards">Short tons to cubic yards</option>
              </select>
            </label>
            {input(
              'amount',
              'Quantity',
              state.fields.direction === 'tons-to-yards' ? 'short tons' : 'yd³',
            )}
            {input(
              'density',
              `${human(material)} density`,
              'short tons/yd³',
              true,
              'Enter the density from your supplier.',
            )}
          </>
        ) : (
          <>
            {state.sections.map((section, index) => (
              <fieldset className="measurement-section" key={index}>
                <legend>Section {index + 1}</legend>
                <div className="field-grid">
                  {(['length', 'width'] as const).map((key) => (
                    <label className="field" key={key}>
                      <span>
                        {key === 'length' ? 'Length' : section.tapered ? 'Start width' : 'Width'}
                      </span>
                      <div className="input-wrap">
                        <input
                          name={`section-${index}-${key}`}
                          type="number"
                          step="any"
                          required
                          value={section[key]}
                          onChange={(e) =>
                            change({
                              ...state,
                              sections: state.sections.map((s, i) =>
                                i === index ? { ...s, [key]: e.target.value } : s,
                              ),
                            })
                          }
                        />
                        <span>ft</span>
                      </div>
                    </label>
                  ))}
                </div>
                <div className="section-options">
                  <label className="check">
                    <input
                      type="checkbox"
                      checked={section.tapered}
                      onChange={(e) =>
                        change({
                          ...state,
                          sections: state.sections.map((s, i) =>
                            i === index ? { ...s, tapered: e.target.checked } : s,
                          ),
                        })
                      }
                    />
                    Tapered width
                  </label>
                  <label className="check">
                    <input
                      type="checkbox"
                      checked={section.sloped}
                      onChange={(e) =>
                        change({
                          ...state,
                          sections: state.sections.map((s, i) =>
                            i === index ? { ...s, sloped: e.target.checked } : s,
                          ),
                        })
                      }
                    />
                    Add slope
                  </label>
                </div>
                {section.tapered && (
                  <label className="field">
                    <span>End width</span>
                    <div className="input-wrap">
                      <input
                        type="number"
                        step="any"
                        required
                        value={section.endWidth}
                        onChange={(e) =>
                          change({
                            ...state,
                            sections: state.sections.map((s, i) =>
                              i === index ? { ...s, endWidth: e.target.value } : s,
                            ),
                          })
                        }
                      />
                      <span>ft</span>
                    </div>
                  </label>
                )}
                {section.sloped && (
                  <div className="field-grid">
                    <label className="field">
                      <span>Grade</span>
                      <div className="input-wrap">
                        <input
                          type="number"
                          step="any"
                          required
                          value={section.grade}
                          onChange={(e) =>
                            change({
                              ...state,
                              sections: state.sections.map((s, i) =>
                                i === index ? { ...s, grade: e.target.value } : s,
                              ),
                            })
                          }
                        />
                        <span>%</span>
                      </div>
                    </label>
                    <label className="field">
                      <span>Length measured</span>
                      <select
                        value={section.measured}
                        onChange={(e) =>
                          change({
                            ...state,
                            sections: state.sections.map((s, i) =>
                              i === index
                                ? { ...s, measured: e.target.value as 'flat' | 'slope' }
                                : s,
                            ),
                          })
                        }
                      >
                        <option value="flat">Along flat ground</option>
                        <option value="slope">Along the slope</option>
                      </select>
                    </label>
                  </div>
                )}
                {state.sections.length > 1 && (
                  <button
                    type="button"
                    className="text-button"
                    onClick={() =>
                      change({ ...state, sections: state.sections.filter((_, i) => i !== index) })
                    }
                  >
                    Remove section {index + 1}
                  </button>
                )}
              </fieldset>
            ))}
            <button
              type="button"
              className="add-section"
              disabled={state.sections.length >= 100}
              onClick={() =>
                change({ ...state, sections: [...state.sections, emptyState().sections[0]] })
              }
            >
              ＋ Add another area
            </button>
            <p className="input-hint">
              Divide an irregular driveway into measured sections. Each section adds to the total
              area.
            </p>
          </>
        )}
        {kind !== 'converter' && (
          <div className="panel-heading subheading">
            <span className="eyebrow">02 / {cost ? 'Cost assumptions' : 'Material inputs'}</span>
          </div>
        )}
        {cost ? (
          <>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Price basis</span>
              <select
                value={state.fields.tier ?? 'baseline'}
                onChange={(e) => field('tier', e.target.value)}
              >
                <option value="baseline">Published benchmark · no regional adjustment</option>
                <option value="low" disabled>
                  Low-cost region · index unavailable
                </option>
                <option value="average" disabled>
                  Average-cost region · index unavailable
                </option>
                <option value="high" disabled>
                  High-cost region · index unavailable
                </option>
              </select>
              <small>
                Baseline uses the published range unchanged. No regional multiplier is assumed.
              </small>
            </label>
            {kind !== 'compare' && (
              <>
                <p className="benchmark-note">
                  {pricingAvailable ? (
                    <>
                      Reference: {currentPrice.installedLow.source}. $
                      {currentPrice.installedLow.value}–${currentPrice.installedHigh.value}/ft².
                      Retrieved {currentPrice.installedLow.retrievedOn}.
                    </>
                  ) : (
                    'Published pricing is unavailable for this scope. Measure area or enter an itemized quote.'
                  )}
                </p>
                {checkbox('customRates', 'Use my quoted unit rates')}
                {state.fields.customRates === 'true' && (
                  <div className="field-grid">
                    {input('unitLow', 'Quoted low rate', 'USD/ft²')}
                    {input('unitHigh', 'Quoted high rate', 'USD/ft²')}
                  </div>
                )}
              </>
            )}
            <details className="optional-inputs">
              <summary>
                Additional quoted work <span>Optional</span>
              </summary>
              <p className="input-hint">
                Add only work excluded from the installed range. Removal and ordinary base work
                already included in a quote stay excluded here.
              </p>
              {checkbox('removal', 'Add separate removal and disposal')}
              {state.fields.removal === 'true' && (
                <div className="field-grid">
                  {input('removalLow', 'Removal low rate', 'USD/ft²', true)}
                  {input('removalHigh', 'Removal high rate', 'USD/ft²', true)}
                </div>
              )}
              {checkbox('base', 'Add separate base preparation')}
              {state.fields.base === 'true' && (
                <div className="field-grid">
                  {input('baseLow', 'Additional base low rate', 'USD/ft²', true)}
                  {input('baseHigh', 'Additional base high rate', 'USD/ft²', true)}
                </div>
              )}
              {checkbox('delivery', 'Add separately quoted delivery')}
              {state.fields.delivery === 'true' && (
                <div className="field-grid">
                  {input('loads', 'Truckload count', 'loads')}
                  {input('deliveryFee', 'Quoted delivery fee', 'USD/load')}
                </div>
              )}
              {(surface === 'concrete' || surface === 'slab') && (
                <>
                  <div className="field-grid">
                    {input('depth', 'Slab thickness', 'in', false)}
                    {input('waste', 'Concrete contingency', '%', false)}
                  </div>
                  {checkbox('shortLoad', 'Check quoted concrete short-load fee')}
                  {state.fields.shortLoad === 'true' && (
                    <div className="field-grid">
                      {input('minimumOrder', 'Supplier minimum', 'yd³')}
                      {input('shortLoadFee', 'Quoted short-load fee', 'USD')}
                    </div>
                  )}
                </>
              )}
            </details>
            {kind !== 'compare' &&
              ['asphalt', 'overlay', 'asphalt-replacement'].includes(surface) && (
                <details className="optional-inputs">
                  <summary>
                    Asphalt material quantity <span>Optional</span>
                  </summary>
                  <div className="field-grid">
                    {input('depth', 'Planned asphalt thickness', 'in', false)}
                    {input('density', 'Producer mix density', 'lb/ft³', false)}
                    {input('waste', 'Quantity allowance', '%', false)}
                  </div>
                  <p className="input-hint">
                    Enter thickness and producer density together. These calculate tonnage
                    separately; they do not invent a price adjustment.
                  </p>
                </details>
              )}
            {kind === 'compare' && (
              <fieldset>
                <legend>Surfaces to compare</legend>
                <div className="surface-choices">
                  {surfaces.map((s) => (
                    <label className="check" key={s}>
                      <input
                        type="checkbox"
                        checked={state.surfaces.includes(s)}
                        onChange={(e) =>
                          change({
                            ...state,
                            surfaces: e.target.checked
                              ? [...state.surfaces, s]
                              : state.surfaces.filter((x) => x !== s),
                            selectedSurface:
                              !e.target.checked && state.selectedSurface === s
                                ? (state.surfaces.find((x) => x !== s) ?? s)
                                : state.selectedSurface,
                          })
                        }
                      />
                      {human(s)}
                    </label>
                  ))}
                </div>
                <fieldset>
                  <legend>Surface of interest</legend>
                  <div className="surface-choices">
                    {surfaces
                      .filter((s) => state.surfaces.includes(s))
                      .map((s) => (
                        <label key={s} className="check">
                          <input
                            type="radio"
                            name="surface-of-interest"
                            value={s}
                            checked={state.selectedSurface === s}
                            onChange={() => change({ ...state, selectedSurface: s })}
                          />
                          {human(s)}
                        </label>
                      ))}
                  </div>
                </fieldset>
                <label className="field">
                  <span>Sort results by</span>
                  <select
                    value={state.sort}
                    onChange={(e) =>
                      change({ ...state, sort: e.target.value as 'upfront' | 'annual' })
                    }
                  >
                    <option value="upfront">Lowest upfront cost</option>
                    <option value="annual">Lowest cost per year of life</option>
                  </select>
                </label>
              </fieldset>
            )}
            <p className="input-hint">
              Estimate only. Installed work and material-only prices cover different scopes.
            </p>
          </>
        ) : kind === 'sealcoat' ? (
          <>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Product coverage reference</span>
              <select
                value={state.fields.product ?? 'custom'}
                onChange={(e) => {
                  const p = sealcoatPresets.find((p) => p.id === e.target.value);
                  change({
                    ...state,
                    fields: {
                      ...state.fields,
                      product: e.target.value,
                      coverage: p?.selectedCoverageSqFtPerGallon
                        ? String(p.selectedCoverageSqFtPerGallon)
                        : '',
                      coats: p?.coats ? String(p.coats) : '',
                      containerSize: p?.containerGallons ? String(p.containerGallons) : '',
                    },
                  });
                }}
              >
                <option value="custom">Enter my product label values</option>
                {sealcoatPresets.map((p) => (
                  <option value={p.id} key={p.id}>
                    {p.name}
                  </option>
                ))}
              </select>
              <small>
                Coverage is per coat. Named references differ by surface condition and product.
                Check your current container label; lower published coverage is used for planning.
              </small>
            </label>
            <div className="field-grid">
              {input('coats', 'Number of coats', 'coats')}
              {input('coverage', 'Label coverage', 'ft²/gal')}
              {input('containerSize', 'Container size', 'gal')}
            </div>
          </>
        ) : kind === 'paver' ? (
          <div className="field-grid">
            {input('paverLength', 'Paver length', 'in')}
            {input('paverWidth', 'Paver width', 'in')}
            {input('waste', 'Waste allowance', '%')}
            {input('baseDepth', 'Base depth', 'in')}
            {input('sandDepth', 'Bedding sand depth', 'in')}
            {input('baseDensity', 'Base density', 'short tons/yd³')}
            {input('sandDensity', 'Sand density', 'short tons/yd³')}
            {input('compaction', 'Base compaction allowance', '%')}
          </div>
        ) : kind !== 'converter' ? (
          <>
            <div className="field-grid">
              {input(
                'depth',
                kind === 'layers' ? 'Surface layer depth' : 'Thickness / depth',
                'in',
              )}
              {input('waste', 'Waste allowance', '%', true, 'Enter 0 to exclude waste.')}
            </div>
            {kind === 'layers' && (
              <div className="field-grid">
                {input('baseDepth', 'Base layer depth', 'in')}
                {input('baseDensity', 'Base density', 'short tons/yd³')}
              </div>
            )}
            {kind !== 'concrete' &&
              input(
                'density',
                kind === 'layers' ? 'Surface density' : `${human(material)} density`,
                kind === 'asphalt' ? 'lb/ft³' : 'short tons/yd³',
                true,
                'Use the density provided by your supplier.',
              )}
            {densityKey && defaultBook[densityKey]?.verified && (
              <p className="input-hint">
                Reference: {defaultBook[densityKey].source}. {defaultBook[densityKey].scope} Every
                value stays editable.
              </p>
            )}
            {(material === 'gravel' || kind === 'layers') && (
              <button
                className="text-button"
                type="button"
                onClick={() => field('density', String(defaultBook.crushedStoneDensity.value))}
              >
                Use Two Rivers 5/8-inch crushed-stone reference: 1.4 short tons/yd³
              </button>
            )}
            {material === 'asphalt millings' && (
              <p className="input-hint">
                Enter a supplier density matching the measured material condition. Stockpile density
                and compacted thickness describe different volumes.
              </p>
            )}
            {(kind === 'gravel' || kind === 'layers') &&
              input(
                'compaction',
                'Compaction allowance',
                '%',
                true,
                'Enter 0 to exclude compaction allowance.',
              )}
            {kind === 'concrete' && (
              <details className="optional-inputs">
                <summary>
                  Bag quantities <span>Optional</span>
                </summary>
                <button
                  type="button"
                  className="text-button"
                  onClick={() =>
                    change({
                      ...state,
                      fields: {
                        ...state.fields,
                        bagSize: '80',
                        bagYield: String(defaultBook.bagYield.value),
                      },
                    })
                  }
                >
                  Use QUIKRETE Concrete Mix 1101 · 80 lb bag reference
                </button>
                <div className="field-grid">
                  {input(
                    'bagSize',
                    'Bag weight',
                    'lb',
                    false,
                    'Weight alone does not set yield. Enter the matching bag-label yield.',
                  )}
                  {input('bagYield', 'Label yield per bag', 'ft³/bag', false)}
                </div>
                <p className="input-hint">The yield printed on the bag determines the bag count.</p>
              </details>
            )}
            <details className="optional-inputs">
              <summary>
                Delivery loads <span>Optional</span>
              </summary>
              {input(
                'capacity',
                'Truck capacity',
                kind === 'concrete' ? 'yd³/load' : 'short tons/load',
                false,
              )}
              <p className="input-hint">
                Enter usable capacity per truckload to calculate the number of loads.
              </p>
            </details>
          </>
        ) : null}
        {!cost && kind !== 'converter' && (
          <p className="input-hint">Use your supplier or product label for material values.</p>
        )}
        {error && (
          <p className="error" role="alert">
            {error}
          </p>
        )}
        <div className="form-actions">
          <button className="button primary" type="submit">
            {cost
              ? pricingAvailable || state.fields.customRates === 'true' || kind === 'compare'
                ? 'Calculate estimate'
                : 'Calculate area'
              : 'Calculate quantity'}{' '}
            <span aria-hidden="true">↗</span>
          </button>
          <button
            className="button secondary"
            type="button"
            onClick={() => {
              change(initialToolState(kind, material));
              history.replaceState(null, '', location.pathname);
            }}
          >
            Reset
          </button>
        </div>
      </form>
      <div
        className="calculator-output"
        ref={outputRef}
        tabIndex={-1}
        role="region"
        aria-label="Calculation result"
      >
        <div className="panel-heading">
          <span className="eyebrow">03 / Your result</span>
          <span className="status-dot">
            {result
              ? result.missing?.length
                ? 'Pricing incomplete'
                : cost
                  ? 'Estimate calculated'
                  : 'Quantity calculated'
              : 'Ready for inputs'}
          </span>
        </div>
        <ResultCard>
          {result ? (
            <>
              <dl className="metrics">
                {result.metrics.map((m) => (
                  <div key={m.label}>
                    <dt>{m.label}</dt>
                    <dd>
                      {m.value}
                      <small>{m.unit}</small>
                    </dd>
                  </div>
                ))}
              </dl>
              {!!result.missing?.length && (
                <div className="data-note">
                  <strong>Price data not loaded</strong>
                  <p>
                    {result.missing.map(human).join(', ')}. The available measurements remain
                    visible; missing price components are excluded from estimates.
                  </p>
                </div>
              )}
              {!!result.rows?.length && (
                <div className="table-scroll">
                  <table>
                    <caption>Estimated surface costs, using the selected assumptions.</caption>
                    <thead>
                      <tr>
                        <th>Surface</th>
                        <th>Estimate</th>
                        <th>Lifespan</th>
                        <th>Cost / year</th>
                        <th>Annual upkeep</th>
                      </tr>
                    </thead>
                    <tbody>
                      {result.rows.map((r) => (
                        <tr key={r.name}>
                          <th>
                            {r.name === 'stamped-concrete'
                              ? 'Basic stamped concrete'
                              : human(r.name)}
                          </th>
                          <td>
                            {money(r.low)}–{money(r.high)}
                          </td>
                          <td>
                            {r.lifespan
                              ? `${number(r.lifespan.low)}–${number(r.lifespan.high)} years`
                              : 'Not available'}
                          </td>
                          <td>
                            {r.annual
                              ? `${money(r.annual.low)}–${money(r.annual.high)}`
                              : 'Not available'}
                          </td>
                          <td>{r.upkeep.length ? r.upkeep.join('; ') : 'Not available'}</td>
                        </tr>
                      ))}
                    </tbody>
                  </table>
                  <p>
                    Cost per year divides the upfront range by the lifespan range; upkeep is
                    separate.
                  </p>
                </div>
              )}
              {cost && (
                <>
                  <p className="estimate-note">
                    Estimate only. This result is not a contractor quote.
                  </p>
                  <div className="result-assumptions">
                    <strong>Assumptions</strong>
                    <p>
                      Price basis:{' '}
                      {state.fields.customRates === 'true'
                        ? 'your quoted rates'
                        : (state.fields.tier ?? 'baseline')}
                      . Removal: {state.fields.removal === 'true' ? 'included' : 'excluded'}. Base
                      work: {state.fields.base === 'true' ? 'included' : 'excluded'}. Delivery:{' '}
                      {state.fields.delivery === 'true' ? 'included' : 'excluded'}.
                    </p>
                    {result.assumptions?.map((a) => (
                      <p key={a}>{a}</p>
                    ))}
                  </div>
                </>
              )}
            </>
          ) : (
            <div className="empty-result">
              {kind === 'converter' ? (
                <div className="conversion-diagram">Volume × density = weight</div>
              ) : (
                <ShapeDiagram tapered={state.sections.some((section) => section.tapered)} />
              )}
              <h3>
                {cost
                  ? 'Your measured area'
                  : kind === 'converter'
                    ? 'Your converted quantity'
                    : 'Your material quantity'}
              </h3>
              <p>
                {kind === 'converter'
                  ? 'Enter a quantity and material density, then calculate.'
                  : cost
                    ? pricingAvailable || kind === 'compare'
                      ? 'Enter your dimensions to estimate installed cost using named published ranges.'
                      : 'Enter your dimensions to calculate area. Pricing is unavailable for this scope.'
                    : 'Enter your dimensions and material inputs, then calculate.'}
              </p>
              <span className="empty-rule">No sign-up · US units</span>
            </div>
          )}
        </ResultCard>
        {result && (
          <>
            <h3 className="worked-inputs">Worked example from your inputs</h3>
            <FormulaBox>
              <code>{result.formula}</code>
              {result.steps.map((step) => (
                <p key={step}>{step}</p>
              ))}
            </FormulaBox>
            <div className="result-actions">
              <button onClick={() => void copy(result.summary)}>Copy result</button>
              <button onClick={() => window.print()}>Print</button>
              <button onClick={share}>Share link</button>
            </div>
            <p className="input-hint" role="status">
              {message}
            </p>
            <QuoteCTA
              area={result.area}
              surface={kind === 'compare' ? state.selectedSurface : surface}
              slug={slug}
            />
          </>
        )}
        {!result && (
          <div className="output-note">
            <span aria-hidden="true">↳</span>
            <p>
              Every result shows its formula.
              <br />
              {cost
                ? 'The range includes the displayed scope and selected extras.'
                : 'Bags, containers, and delivery loads round up.'}
            </p>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

## components/DraftGuidance.tsx

````tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import { FormulaBox, QASection } from './Modules';
import type { ToolKind } from '@/lib/calc/ui';

export default function DraftGuidance({
  kind,
  costGuide,
  currentUrl,
}: {
  kind: ToolKind | null;
  costGuide: boolean;
  currentUrl: string;
}) {
  if (kind === 'cost' || kind === 'compare' || costGuide) {
    return (
      <QASection question="How do you prepare a cost estimate?">
        <p>
          <strong>Start with measured area and an itemized supplier or contractor quote.</strong>{' '}
          Match each rate to the unit on that quote.
        </p>
        <div className="table-scroll">
          <table>
            <caption>Information to collect for a driveway quote</caption>
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th>Input</th>
                <th>Record</th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              <tr>
                <th>Project size</th>
                <td>Length and width in feet; measure separate sections individually.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <th>Surface work</th>
                <td>Quoted rate and its unit, such as dollars per square foot.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <th>Preparation</th>
                <td>Separate removal, base work, grading, and repair charges.</td>
              </tr>
              <tr>
                <th>Delivery and minimums</th>
                <td>Delivery fees and any minimum order or project charge.</td>
              </tr>
            </tbody>
          </table>
        </div>
        <p>
          For material-only quotes, use the supplier’s weight or volume unit. Installed-work rates
          and material-only rates cover different work.
        </p>
        <p>
          Published price ranges are awaiting verified source data.{' '}
          {currentUrl === '/driveway-cost-calculator/' ? (
            'The calculator above calculates measured area while that pricing is unavailable.'
          ) : (
            <>
              The <Link href="/driveway-cost-calculator/">Driveway Cost Calculator</Link> calculates
              measured area while that pricing is unavailable.
            </>
          )}
        </p>
      </QASection>
    );
  }
  if (!kind) return null;
  const rows: [string, string, string][] =
    kind === 'converter'
      ? [
          ['Quantity', 'yd³ or short tons', 'Choose the conversion direction.'],
          ['Material density', 'short tons/yd³', 'Use the value supplied for your material.'],
        ]
      : [
          ['Length and width', 'ft', 'Measure each section. For a taper, enter both end widths.'],
          ...(kind === 'sealcoat'
            ? ([
                ['Coverage', 'ft²/gal', 'Use the coverage rate printed on the product label.'],
                ['Coats', 'count', 'Enter the number of coats in your plan.'],
                [
                  'Container size',
                  'gal',
                  'Enter the amount in one container to calculate container count.',
                ],
              ] as [string, string, string][])
            : kind === 'paver'
              ? ([
                  ['Paver dimensions', 'in', 'Enter the length and width of one paver.'],
                  [
                    'Base and bedding',
                    'in; short tons/yd³',
                    'Use your planned depths and supplier densities.',
                  ],
                ] as [string, string, string][])
              : ([
                  ['Depth', 'in', 'Enter your planned material thickness.'],
                  ...(kind === 'concrete'
                    ? []
                    : [
                        [
                          'Density',
                          kind === 'asphalt' ? 'lb/ft³' : 'short tons/yd³',
                          'Get the density for this material from your supplier.',
                        ],
                      ]),
                ] as [string, string, string][])),
          ...(kind === 'sealcoat'
            ? []
            : ([['Allowances', '%', 'Enter your project allowance; enter 0 to exclude it.']] as [
                string,
                string,
                string,
              ][])),
          ...(kind === 'concrete'
            ? ([
                [
                  'Bag yield (optional)',
                  'ft³/bag',
                  'Use the yield on the bag to calculate bag count.',
                ],
              ] as [string, string, string][])
            : []),
        ];
  return (
    <QASection question="Which inputs does this calculator use?">
      <p>
        <strong>Your measurements and supplier values determine the result.</strong> Material values
        start blank. Enter the density, yield, or coverage for the product you are ordering.
      </p>
      <div className="table-scroll">
        <table>
          <caption>Input units and where to find each value</caption>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Input</th>
              <th>Unit</th>
              <th>How to enter it</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {rows.map(([label, unit, note]) => (
              <tr key={label}>
                <th>{label}</th>
                <td>{unit}</td>
                <td>{note}</td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      {kind !== 'converter' && kind !== 'sealcoat' && kind !== 'paver' && (
        <FormulaBox>
          Volume in cubic yards = area in square feet × (depth in inches ÷ 12) ÷ 27. Waste and
          compaction allowances apply only when entered.
        </FormulaBox>
      )}
    </QASection>
  );
}
````

import Link from 'next/link';
import { pages } from '@/lib/content';
import Navigation from './Navigation';
const groups = [

## components/Navigation.tsx

````tsx
'use client';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
type Group = { label: string; links: { href: string; label: string }[] };
export default function Navigation({ groups }: { groups: Group[] }) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const nav = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (open === null) return;
    function outside(event: PointerEvent) {
      if (event.target instanceof Node && !nav.current?.contains(event.target)) setOpen(null);
    }
    function escape(event: KeyboardEvent) {
      if (event.key !== 'Escape') return;
      setOpen(null);
      nav.current?.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(`[data-nav-trigger="${open}"]`)?.focus();
    }
    document.addEventListener('pointerdown', outside);
    document.addEventListener('keydown', escape);
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener('pointerdown', outside);
      document.removeEventListener('keydown', escape);
    };
  }, [open]);
  return (
    <nav
      ref={nav}
      aria-label="Main navigation"
      onBlur={(event) => {
        if (
          event.relatedTarget instanceof Node &&
          !event.currentTarget.contains(event.relatedTarget)
        )
          setOpen(null);
      }}
    >
      {groups.map((group, index) => (
        <div className="nav-group" key={group.label}>
          <button
            type="button"
            className="nav-trigger"
            data-nav-trigger={index}
            aria-expanded={open === index}
            aria-controls={`main-menu-${index}`}
            onClick={() => setOpen(open === index ? null : index)}
          >
            {group.label}
            <span aria-hidden="true">⌄</span>
          </button>
          <div className="nav-dropdown" id={`main-menu-${index}`} hidden={open !== index}>
            {group.links.map((link) => (
              <Link key={link.href} href={link.href} onClick={() => setOpen(null)}>
                {link.label}
              </Link>
            ))}
          </div>
        </div>
      ))}
      <Link className="nav-about" href="/about/" onClick={() => setOpen(null)}>
        About
      </Link>
    </nav>
  );
}
````

## components/QuoteCTA.tsx

````tsx
'use client';
import { useEffect, useState, useRef, type FormEvent } from 'react';
import Link from 'next/link';
import { FLAGS } from '@/lib/config';
import { track } from '@/lib/analytics';
type Config = {
  consent: string;
  success: string;
  phone: string;
  phoneRequired: boolean;
  turnstileSiteKey: string;
};
declare global {
  interface Window {
    turnstile?: {
      render: (el: HTMLElement, opts: Record<string, unknown>) => string;
      remove: (id: string) => void;
    };
    onDrivewayTurnstile?: () => void;
  }
}
export default function QuoteCTA({
  area,
  surface,
  slug,
}: {
  area?: number;
  surface: string;
  slug: string;
}) {
  const requestId = useRef<string | null>(null);
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const [config, setConfig] = useState<Config | null>(null);
  const [token, setToken] = useState('');
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('');
  const [busy, setBusy] = useState(false);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!FLAGS.leads || !open) return;
    let active = true;
    fetch('/api/lead')
      .then((r) => (r.ok ? r.json() : null))
      .then((c) => {
        if (active) setConfig(c);
      })
      .catch(() => setStatus('Quote requests are unavailable.'));
    return () => {
      active = false;
    };
  }, [open]);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!config || !open) return;
    let widget: string | undefined;
    let removed = false;
    const init = () => {
      const el = document.getElementById('quote-turnstile');
      if (el && !removed && window.turnstile)
        widget = window.turnstile.render(el, {
          sitekey: config.turnstileSiteKey,
          action: 'quote',
          callback: (t: string) => setToken(t),
          'expired-callback': () => setToken(''),
        });
    };
    if (window.turnstile) init();
    else {
      window.onDrivewayTurnstile = init;
      const script = document.createElement('script');
      script.src =
        'https://challenges.cloudflare.com/turnstile/v0/api.js?onload=onDrivewayTurnstile&render=explicit';
      script.async = true;
      document.head.appendChild(script);
    }
    return () => {
      removed = true;
      if (widget) window.turnstile?.remove(widget);
    };
  }, [config, open]);
  if (!FLAGS.leads) return null;
  async function submit(e: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    if (busy || !config) return;
    const form = e.currentTarget;
    setBusy(true);
    setStatus('');
    try {
      const fields = Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form));
      requestId.current ??= crypto.randomUUID();
      const res = await fetch('/api/lead', {
        method: 'POST',
        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
        body: JSON.stringify({
          ...fields,
          area: Number(fields.area),
          consent: fields.consent === 'on',
          token,
          idempotencyKey: requestId.current,
          pageUrl: location.origin + location.pathname,
        }),
      });
      if (!res.ok)
        throw new Error(
          res.status === 429
            ? 'Too many requests. Try again later.'
            : 'The request was not accepted. Check the fields and try again.',
        );
      setStatus(config.success);
      setOpen(false);
    } catch (e) {
      setStatus(e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Request failed.');
    } finally {
      setBusy(false);
    }
  }
  return (
    <aside className="quote-cta">
      <h3>Get free driveway quotes</h3>
      <p>Share your project details with the approved quote network.</p>
      <button
        className="button primary"
        onClick={() => {
          setOpen(!open);
          track('quote_cta_viewed', slug);
          track('quote_cta_clicked', slug);
        }}
      >
        {open ? 'Close form' : 'Request quotes'}
      </button>
      {open && config && (
        <form onSubmit={submit} className="quote-form">
          <div className="field-grid">
            <label className="field">
              <span>ZIP code</span>
              <input name="zip" required pattern="[0-9]{5}" inputMode="numeric" maxLength={5} />
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Project type</span>
              <select name="project">
                <option value="new">New</option>
                <option value="replace">Replace</option>
                <option value="resurface">Resurface</option>
                <option value="repair">Repair</option>
                <option value="seal">Seal</option>
              </select>
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Surface</span>
              <select
                name="surface"
                defaultValue={
                  ['asphalt', 'concrete', 'gravel', 'pavers'].includes(surface)
                    ? surface
                    : 'not-sure'
                }
              >
                {['asphalt', 'concrete', 'gravel', 'pavers', 'not-sure'].map((s) => (
                  <option key={s}>{s}</option>
                ))}
              </select>
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Approximate size (ft²)</span>
              <input name="area" type="number" step="any" required min="0.01" defaultValue={area} />
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Timeline</span>
              <select name="timeline">
                <option value="within-1-month">Within 1 month</option>
                <option value="1-to-3-months">1 to 3 months</option>
                <option value="researching">Researching</option>
              </select>
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>First name</span>
              <input name="firstName" required maxLength={100} />
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Email</span>
              <input name="email" type="email" required />
            </label>
            <label className="field">
              <span>Phone{config.phoneRequired ? '' : ' (optional)'}</span>
              <input name="phone" type="tel" required={config.phoneRequired} />
            </label>
          </div>
          <label className="honeypot" aria-hidden="true">
            Website
            <input name="website" tabIndex={-1} autoComplete="off" />
          </label>
          <label className="check">
            <input name="consent" type="checkbox" required />
            {config.consent}
          </label>
          <div id="quote-turnstile" />
          <p>
            <Link href="/privacy/">Privacy policy</Link>
          </p>
          <button className="button primary" disabled={busy || !token}>
            {busy ? 'Sending…' : 'Submit request'}
          </button>
        </form>
      )}
      {status && <p role="status">{status}</p>}
      {config?.phone && (
        <a className="mobile-call" href={'tel:' + config.phone}>
          Call for quotes
        </a>
      )}
      <p className="disclosure">
        Driveway Calculators receives payment for accepted quote requests.
      </p>
    </aside>
  );
}
````

## components/ResearchModules.tsx

````tsx
import Link from 'next/link';
import { priceBook, defaultBook, verifiedValue } from '@/lib/data';
import { computeCost, computeCompare, computeConversion } from '@/lib/calc';
import { number, money, rateMoney } from '@/lib/format';
import sources from '@/data/sources.json';
import research from '@/data/research/register.json';
const names: Record<string, string> = {
  asphalt: 'New asphalt',
  concrete: 'Standard concrete',
  'stamped-concrete': 'Basic stamped concrete',
  gravel: 'Gravel',
  pavers: 'Pavers',
  'tar-and-chip': 'Tar and chip',
  slab: 'Flat slab',
  sealcoating: 'Sealcoating',
  millings: 'Millings',
  overlay: 'Asphalt overlay',
  'asphalt-replacement': 'Asphalt replacement',
  'concrete-replacement': 'Concrete replacement',
  repair: 'Asphalt hot patch',
  'concrete-repair': 'Concrete resurfacing',
};
export function CostReference({ surface }: { surface: string }) {
  const p = priceBook[surface];
  const low = verifiedValue(p?.installedLow),
    high = verifiedValue(p?.installedHigh);
  if (low === null || high === null)
    return <p>Pricing for this scope remains unavailable. Use an itemized local quote.</p>;
  const sample = computeCost({ area: 400, unit: { low, high }, tier: 1, extras: [] })!;
  return (
    <section className="reference-panel">
      <h2>Which published range does the estimate use?</h2>
      <p>
        <strong>
          {names[surface] ?? surface}: {rateMoney(low)}–{rateMoney(high)} per square foot.
        </strong>{' '}
        {surface === 'concrete-replacement' ? (
          'This range is derived from the separate installation and demolition components; it is not an observed replacement quote.'
        ) : (
          <>
            This named benchmark is preserved from {p.installedLow.source}; competing guides are not
            averaged.
          </>
        )}
      </p>
      <div className="table-scroll">
        <table>
          <caption>Published rate and an illustrative measurement</caption>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Basis</th>
              <th>Low</th>
              <th>High</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr>
              <th>Installed work / ft²</th>
              <td>{rateMoney(low)}</td>
              <td>{rateMoney(high)}</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
              <th>20 × 20 ft example · 400 ft²</th>
              <td>{money(sample.low)}</td>
              <td>{money(sample.high)}</td>
            </tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <p>
        The example is generated by the cost engine with no regional adjustment or additional
        charges. Site conditions, work inclusions, and local quotes determine the project total.{' '}
        {surface.includes('replacement')
          ? 'Removal is included in this replacement basis; do not add it twice.'
          : 'Add separately quoted work only when excluded from the installed scope.'}
      </p>
      <p className="source-caption">
        Retrieved {p.installedLow.retrievedOn}. Source comparisons and exclusions:{' '}
        <Link href="/methodology/">Methodology</Link>.
      </p>
    </section>
  );
}
export function SurfaceComparison({ pairOnly = false }: { pairOnly?: boolean }) {
  const allKeys = ['asphalt', 'concrete', 'stamped-concrete', 'gravel', 'pavers', 'tar-and-chip'];
  const keys = pairOnly ? ['asphalt', 'concrete'] : allKeys;
  const rows = computeCompare(
    400,
    1,
    keys.map((name) => {
      const p = priceBook[name];
      return {
        name,
        unit: { low: p.installedLow.value!, high: p.installedHigh.value! },
        lifespan:
          p.lifespanLow.value !== null && p.lifespanHigh.value !== null
            ? { low: p.lifespanLow.value, high: p.lifespanHigh.value }
            : null,
        extras: [],
        upkeep: [],
      };
    }),
  ).rows;
  return (
    <section className="reference-panel">
      <h2>How do published surface ranges compare?</h2>
      <p>
        <strong>Compare the same measured area and the same included work.</strong> These are
        different publishers’ benchmarks, not local bids collected for one project.
      </p>
      <div className="table-scroll">
        <table>
          <caption>400 ft² illustrative comparison · no extras or regional adjustment</caption>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Surface</th>
              <th>Installed / ft²</th>
              <th>400 ft² example</th>
              <th>Service-life reference</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {rows.map((r) => (
              <tr key={r.name}>
                <th>{names[r.name]}</th>
                <td>
                  {rateMoney(priceBook[r.name].installedLow.value!)}–
                  {rateMoney(priceBook[r.name].installedHigh.value!)}
                </td>
                <td>
                  {money(r.low)}–{money(r.high)}
                </td>
                <td>
                  {r.lifespan
                    ? `${r.lifespan.low}–${r.lifespan.high} years`
                    : 'No comparable bounded range'}
                </td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <p>
        Service life depends on construction and maintenance. Upfront cost divided by service life
        excludes maintenance, financing, and future replacement. Gravel remains renewable through
        replenishment, so a fixed life denominator is omitted.
      </p>
    </section>
  );
}
export function MaterialReferences({ material }: { material?: string }) {
  const allKeys = [
    'asphaltDensity',
    'rockDensity',
    'peaGravelDensity',
    'crusherRunDensity',
    'roadBaseDensity',
    'concreteDensity',
  ];
  const selection: Record<string, string[]> = {
    asphalt: ['asphaltDensity'],
    millings: ['millingsBulkDensity'],
    gravel: ['crushedStoneDensity'],
    layers: ['roadBaseDensity', 'crushedStoneDensity'],
    rock: ['rockDensity'],
    pea: ['peaGravelDensity'],
    crusher: ['crusherRunDensity'],
    base: ['roadBaseDensity'],
    concrete: ['concreteDensity'],
  };
  const keys = material && selection[material] ? selection[material] : allKeys;
  return (
    <section className="reference-panel">
      <h2>Which material density references are available?</h2>
      <p>
        <strong>Density follows the named material and its condition.</strong> Loose stockpile,
        compacted paving, and cured concrete values describe different volumes.
      </p>
      <div className="table-scroll">
        <table>
          <caption>Named editable material references</caption>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th>Reference</th>
              <th>Value</th>
              <th>Source and scope</th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {keys.map((k) => {

              return (
                <tr key={k}>
                  <th>{k.replace(/([A-Z])/g, ' $1')}</th>
                  <td>
                    {number(d.value!)} {d.unit}
                  </td>
                  <td>
                    {d.source}. {d.scope}
                  </td>
                </tr>
              );
            })}
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
      <p>
        Replace a reference with the density supplied for your order. Moisture, size grading, voids,
        and compaction change bulk density.{' '}
        <Link href="/material-weights/">Material Weight Chart</Link> connects these inputs to the
        quantity tools.
      </p>
    </section>
  );
}
export function WeightReference({ material }: { material: 'concrete' | 'gravel' }) {
  const density =
    material === 'concrete'
      ? defaultBook.concreteDensity.value!
      : (defaultBook.crushedStoneDensity.value! * 2000) / 27;
  const weight = computeConversion({
    amount: 1,
    density: (density * 27) / 2000,
    direction: 'yards-to-tons',
  });
  return (
    <section className="reference-panel">
      <h2>How does density determine weight per cubic yard?</h2>
      <p>
        <strong>Weight per cubic yard equals density per cubic foot × 27.</strong> At the named{' '}
        {material === 'concrete'
          ? 'NRMCA normalweight reference'
          : 'Two Rivers 5/8-inch crushed-stone reference'}
        , one cubic yard is {number(weight.tons * 2000)} lb, or {number(weight.tons)} US short tons.
      </p>
      <p>
        The result is calculated from the selected reference. Dry bagged concrete, cured
        normalweight concrete, lightweight concrete, and loose crushed concrete are separate
        materials. Supplier-specific gravel density replaces a universal weight assumption.
      </p>
    </section>
  );
}

export function RepairReference() {

## How to calculate asphalt tonnage?

**Multiply area by thickness divided by 12 and by density, then divide by 2,000.**

The complete formula is tons = area × (thickness / 12) × density / 2,000. A short ton (2,000 lb) is the US mass unit used here. An asphalt tonnage calculator handles these unit changes without treating inches as feet. Calculate the asphalt surface and each asphalt base course separately when their depths or mix densities differ.

## How do you choose asphalt density and thickness?

**Use the supplier’s in-place density and the finished compacted thickness.**

The Asphalt Institute publishes an in-place density range of 142–148 lb per cubic foot and uses 148 for quantity estimates. Craig Paving uses 148; the Minnesota Asphalt Pavement Association uses a compacted spread factor of 110 lb per square yard per inch. These named assumptions differ. The editable starting density follows the Asphalt Institute rather than averaging the sources. Colorado Asphalt Pavement Association guidance uses 3 inches of asphalt over an aggregate base for its residential design. Its full-depth asphalt sections are separate designs, so this asphalt driveway calculator does not choose an engineered pavement section for your site.

## How to figure asphalt tonnage for a tapered driveway?

**Use the average of the start and end widths to calculate the footprint.**

Figuring asphalt for a taper uses area = length × (start width + end width) / 2. Measure along the paved slope or enter a flat distance with grade; avoid adjusting a slope measurement a second time. For curves and irregular aprons, divide the footprint into measured sections and add their results. The how-to-measure steps explain how to figure out asphalt tonnage from those separate areas.

## How to calculate tons of asphalt to order?

**Apply your entered waste allowance to the calculated quantity, then round up to the purchase increment.**

Compaction is already represented by compacted thickness and in-place density. Adding another automatic compaction multiplier counts that change twice. Zero waste allowance excludes extra material; it does not recommend an exact order. Ask the plant to confirm the order increment, truck payload and access. Delivery load rounding is separate from the amount of material in the pavement. The unrounded figure explains how to figure tons of asphalt; the rounded figure is the purchasing quantity.

## Does this asphalt calculator online calculate bitumen alone?

**This tool estimates the whole asphalt mixture, including aggregate and binder.**

A bitumen calculator for binder-only quantities requires the specified binder proportion; that is a different input from total hot mix weight. Use the [Asphalt Driveway Cost Calculator](/asphalt-driveway-cost-calculator/) to price the driveway area, and the [Asphalt Driveway Thickness](/asphalt-driveway-thickness/) to understand the layer that drives tonnage. The [Material Weight Chart](/material-weights/) documents the selected density.

<MaterialReferences material="asphalt" />

The formula answers “how do you calculate asphalt tonnage?” using measured area, thickness, density, and the entered allowance. The same inputs remain in the share link and printed result.
````

## Which product instructions control the repair?

**Use the directions on the actual bag rather than a universal pothole recipe.**

QUIKRETE Permanent Blacktop Repair describes applications 1–3 inches thick in compacted 1-inch lifts, with repairs limited to about 3 × 3 feet. Sakrete Blacktop Patch’s linked sheet limits repairs to 2 × 2 feet and 4 inches deep. These different limits are not combined into a larger permitted repair.

## How much material does a bag yield?

**Bag yield describes the compacted repair volume, not the driveway area alone.**

QUIKRETE lists about 0.5 cubic foot from a 50-pound bag and about 0.6 cubic foot from a 60-pound bag. Measure the pothole area and depth before comparing package quantities. Loose material appearance does not establish compacted yield. No project bag count is calculated manually in this guide; a generated quantity example requires the matching engine and input specification.

## What does compaction do in the procedure?

**Compaction forms each placed layer into the specified repair.**

QUIKRETE’s instructions require adequately compacted lifts. Sakrete describes placing a 2-inch loose layer and compacting it to 1 inch before repeating. Those directions apply to the named products; do not transfer the loose-depth conversion to another material. Clear the damaged area and follow the selected preparation instructions, then respect the package’s opening-to-traffic requirements.

## Is every cold patch only a temporary repair?

**Repair performance depends on the product and the underlying defect.**

A generic temporary repair description does not erase a manufacturer’s named permanent-repair claim or prove its performance at every site. The reviewed sources establish no universal cold-patch lifespan. Recurrent potholes, alligator cracking, and sinking need attention to the support and drainage. The asphalt driveway repair cost guide distinguishes cold patch, hot patch, and full-depth repairs. Compare three details before buying: permitted dimensions, compacted yield, and application method. Keep the bag label and repair photographs with the maintenance record.

## How are cracks, patches, and potholes priced?

**Crack length and patch area use different units.**

Measure each damaged area before requesting a quote. HomeGuide reports $100–$400 per pothole, while Angi groups method-dependent patches at $100–$500. Those project figures do not convert directly into a square-foot rate without a defined area and depth. Ask whether the quoted total includes the crew’s service minimum and whether multiple repairs share that mobilization charge.

## What is the difference between cold patch and hot patch?

**Cold patch uses a packaged repair mix; hot patch uses hot asphalt placed and compacted by a paving crew.**

Product instructions govern the repair depth, lift thickness, and compaction method for a packaged mix. A cold patch figure covers that repair method, not new driveway installation. HomeGuide’s hot-patch benchmark is a method-specific area price. Keep the material bag price, patching labor, and complete job quote separate when comparing bids.

## Does crack filler repair alligator cracking?

**A crack filler seals a crack; it does not replace a failed pavement foundation.**

Blacktop Concepts identifies interconnected cracking, sinking, and repeated potholes as reasons to inspect the base and drainage. Alligator cracking describes a connected pattern rather than a single measured line. Record its affected area and take photographs for the contractor. Adding sealer over that pattern does not establish a structural repair specification.

## When does replacement enter the comparison?

**Replacement enters the comparison when damage extends beyond isolated repair areas.**

Compare three scope items: removal of failed material, correction beneath the surface, and replacement pavement thickness. A repair estimate needs the same clarity as a repaving estimate. The crack filler guide covers compatible materials, and the asphalt cold patch guide explains product limits. The repaving guide distinguishes overlay from tear-out. Choose the comparison that matches the actual failure instead of applying one repair price to the whole driveway.

Sealing maintains the surface; it does not replace patching a failed area or repairing the base.

````

## Is every driveway built to the same thickness?

**Asphalt driveway thickness depends on the design, traffic load, and supporting ground.**

CAPA’s technical brief distinguishes asphalt over an aggregate base from full-depth asphalt construction. Harrison Paving and Nathan’s Paving describe regional passenger-car designs using 2–3 inches of compacted asphalt over a granular base. These are named design examples, not one nationwide requirement. Confirm the planned section with the contractor before estimating tons.

## How does base thickness differ from asphalt thickness?

**Base course and asphalt layers are separate parts of the pavement section.**

CAPA’s example uses a 4-inch aggregate base for fair or good subgrade and a 6-inch base for poor subgrade. Do not enter the combined pavement depth as the asphalt thickness. Record the base material separately from the asphalt mix. The subgrade is the supporting ground beneath those layers; weak areas and drainage concerns require attention in the project design.

## Does the calculator use loose or compacted depth?

**Use final compacted asphalt depth with the calculator’s in-place density assumption.**

The Asphalt Institute publishes an estimated mixture density range of 142–148 pounds per cubic foot. Its named 148-pound value is editable. Combining final volume with in-place density already describes compacted material; another automatic compaction multiplier counts that adjustment twice. A supplier’s order allowance is a separate explicit input, not a substitute for specifying the pavement section.

## What belongs in a paving quote?

**The quote needs the asphalt section, base section, and preparation scope.**

Check three details: the thickness after compaction, the material and depth beneath it, and the treatment of soft or poorly drained areas. A paving price without those details is difficult to compare. The asphalt calculator turns specified thickness and measurements into tons. The asphalt driveway cost guide separates that material quantity from installed pricing. Keep project drawings and contractor recommendations with the saved estimate so the assumptions remain visible.

## How do you calculate asphalt millings?

**Volume equals area × depth in feet, and tons equal cubic yards × the selected tons-per-yard factor.**

Divide cubic feet by 27 for cubic yards. Keep the finished layer depth separate from the loose quantity delivered. Reclaimed asphalt pavement retains asphalt binder and aggregate, but its delivered stockpile weight is different from the in-place density of fresh hot mix.

## Which density belongs to millings?

**Use the supplier’s factor for the delivered material and its stated condition.**

Anchorage Sand & Gravel lists 1-inch-minus RAP at about 2,800 lb per cubic yard, or 1.4 US short tons. It identifies these as stockpile weights that vary with moisture, texture and gradation. Lasalle lists millings and screened millings at 2,500 lb per yard, equivalent to 1.25 tons. Hello Gravel uses 1.4 as its planning conversion. The calculator’s named reference is editable; the difference between suppliers stays visible.

## How does compaction change the order?

**Compaction changes the volume relationship, so use a documented allowance for the actual product.**

A stockpile conversion applied to a compacted finished volume needs the supplier’s loose-to-finished adjustment. Do not add the same allowance twice. Zero excludes an extra adjustment; it is not a recommendation for uncompacted construction. FHWA publishes separate processed-RAP and compacted-density observations. Those conditions do not form one interchangeable default.

## What needs checking before delivery?

**Confirm gradation, depth condition, purchase increment, truck capacity and the drop location.**

Ask whether the supplier sells screened or unscreened material and whether its quote is per ton or per yard. Use the [Asphalt Millings Cost](/asphalt-millings-cost/) for driveway installation scope. Use the [Asphalt Calculator](/asphalt-calculator/) for fresh hot mix, whose compacted density and quantity assumptions differ.

## What are you buying when you order millings?

**Asphalt millings are reclaimed asphalt pavement used as a granular material.**

The material comes from processed existing pavement rather than a fresh hot-mix production run. Product size, screening, and condition affect the order. Ask the supplier to identify the grade and whether its ton means a US short ton. A material quote does not automatically include spreading, base preparation, roller compaction, or delivery to your driveway.

## How do supplier prices compare?

**Each published supplier price describes a local product and pickup arrangement.**

UCS in Milltown, Wisconsin, lists recycled asphalt at $15 per ton FOB, excluding tax. Sargent’s Hermon, Maine, list has reclaim/recycled HMA at $20 per ton FOB. Yarberry in Anderson, Indiana, lists millings at $23 per ton without stated delivery inclusion. These examples are not combined into a national delivered price, and availability requires supplier confirmation.

## What changes the installed driveway price?

**Preparation, hauling, and compaction distinguish an installed quote from a material purchase.**

HomeGuide’s $2–$5 benchmark differs from Angi’s $3–$8 and Fragale’s Connecticut $1–$3 example. Compare three inclusions: the prepared base, delivery to the site, and finished compaction. Ask how transitions and runoff are handled. A cheap stockpile is not a finished driveway, and a thick loose layer is not the same measurement as final compacted depth.

## How much material does your driveway need?

**Use the millings calculator with the measured area, depth, and an identified bulk density.**

The Anchorage supplier preset is a named ordering assumption, not a universal density. Keep any supplier compaction allowance explicit so it is not added twice. The gravel driveway cost guide provides the adjacent loose-surface comparison. Upkeep includes watching for rutting and drainage problems; no complete annual maintenance price is established by the reviewed sources. Material quotes use US short tons. Base depth and drainage condition affect the required construction scope; millings tons alone do not price grading and compaction.

## How to calculate concrete yards?

**Multiply area by thickness in feet and divide by 27.**

The concrete slab calculator uses the flat slab footprint and its finished thickness. A concrete pad calculator follows the same geometry; thicker edges or separate footings need their own measured quantities. To understand how to calculate yards of concrete for an irregular outline, calculate its sections and add their volumes. The answer to “how do I calculate yards of concrete?” comes from those dimensions, not the dry weight printed on a bag.

## How do you calculate how much concrete you need?

**Use the measured volume plus the selected ordering allowance.**

Waste allowance accounts for your chosen contingency, while thickness remains the project design. NRMCA discusses ordering additional material; the selected source guidance stays visible. A zero allowance excludes extra volume rather than recommending an exact-volume purchase. This material calculator for a concrete slab does not select reinforcement, strength, joint layout or a structural design.

## How many bags of concrete do I need?

**Divide the required cubic feet by the exact product yield and round up to whole bags.**

The concrete bag calculator uses finished mixed yield, not bag mass divided by a generic concrete density. QUIKRETE Concrete Mix 1101 lists about 0.60 cubic foot for its 80 lb bag. Sakrete’s matching product information provides a cross-check, while other product sizes retain their own label yields. A bag-concrete calculator needs the product name as well as nominal bag weight. The rounded bag count is separate from the unrounded volume.

## How does this concrete calculator for a slab handle delivery?

**Ready-mix uses a cubic-yard order and bagged concrete uses a full-bag count.**

A concrete yards calculator does not turn a supplier’s short-load billing minimum into physical concrete required. Enter the actual minimum and fee where relevant, and confirm pour access and unloading arrangements with the supplier. A concrete calculator with bags is useful for comparing packaged material with ready-mix volume, but those purchase units have different logistics.

## What needs checking before a concrete order?

**Confirm the slab dimensions, finished depth, selected mix and purchase rounding.**

For a concrete calculator used for a slab, keep each thicker section distinct from the flat field. The [Concrete Driveway Cost Calculator](/concrete-driveway-cost-calculator/) prices driveway scope, while the [Concrete Driveway Cost in 2026](/concrete-driveway-cost/) explains labor and preparation around the measured volume. A bags-of-concrete calculation alone excludes those installation charges.

**The cost of concrete driveway installation starts with area multiplied by an installed square-foot range, rather than the delivered concrete price alone.**

HomeGuide’s standard range is $6–$10 per square foot. Concrete Network lists plain gray concrete at $5–$8, while Angi separates plain finishes at $6–$8 from broom finishes at $8–$12. These scopes differ; Driveway Calculators uses HomeGuide’s named standard benchmark without averaging them. Compare the concrete slab, slab thickness, reinforcement, formwork, finish, control joints, and subbase described in each proposal.

## How much is a concrete driveway per square foot?

**The price per square foot includes installation work, whereas a price per cubic yard describes the ready-mix material.**

Slab thickness changes cubic yards. Rebar and wire mesh describe reinforcement; the quote identifies the reinforcement specified for the job. Ask whether formwork, subbase preparation, curing, sealing, and hauling are included. Our [Concrete Driveway Cost Calculator](/concrete-driveway-cost-calculator/) applies measurements to the selected price range and reports quantity separately.

The installed benchmark includes the pour and finishing, rather than just the truck’s concrete. The [Stamped Concrete Driveway Cost](/stamped-concrete-driveway-cost/) prices pattern and color separately from a plain finish.
